note: ⚠ Unverified estimate — not confirmed against official spec documents or real app screenshots. Before relying on this in production, re-measure UI element coordinates (caption area / like-share buttons / profile / progress bar) from real TikTok/Shorts/Reels screenshots and update the top/bottom/left/right values below. The goal isn't to provide 'the correct coordinates' but to 'track evidence and confidence' — also check each platform's confidence/source/note fields.

tiktok.note: No official fixed pixel spec for organic video. Based on ad template references.
tiktok.source: TikTok Ads Manager's official docs also state that 'safe zone size depends on caption length/ad format' instead of giving fixed numbers, and only provide downloadable safe zone template files (zip). There's no official spec at all for organic (non-ad) video — the current coordinates are an engineering estimate based on several creator tools/blogs.

shorts.note: No fixed safe zone per YouTube's official guide. Provided dynamically in the app's editing UI.
shorts.source: YouTube's official Help Center docs: guide lines are shown in real time on screen, positioned to match UI elements like like/comment/description when you move text/stickers — no fixed pixel/percent values are officially published. The structure fundamentally can't be fully expressed as a static config value. Current coordinates are an engineering estimate.

reels.note: Official Meta Ads numbers exist, but since they're an ads spec with no guarantee of matching the organic Reels UI, classified as conservative_estimate.
reels.source: Meta's official Ads Help Center states top 14% / bottom 35% / sides 6% each for Reels ads (top≈269px, bottom≈672px, left/right≈65px on a 1080x1920 base) — the only official fixed number confirmed among the three platforms. However, this is an ads safe zone that includes CTA/product tags, so it may be set wider than the organic post UI. As of research time, no official spec was found for the organic Reels UI itself — the top/bottom/left/right below keep the existing engineering estimate.
